memos.headline: AAPL and UNH Lead on Relative Strength; AMZN and MSFT Show Deteriorating Momentum
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AAPL (+9.3% vs 50d, +15.9% vs 200d, only -2.5% from 52w high) and UNH (+14.3% vs 50d, +40% over 12w, RSI 68.3 near highs) are the strongest trend names, with AAPL showing the cleanest profile—strong relative strength vs SPY (+6.1% 4w, +8.8% 12w) and moderate RSI leaving room to run. CAT has been a monster (+57.6% over 26w, +39.6% vs 200d) but is now extremely extended and I'd want to see a pullback before adding. On the weak side, AMZN's RSI at 37.8 with -9.1% in a week and -10.1% relative strength vs SPY over 4w signals active distribution, while MSFT sits -23.1% from its 52w high and below its 200d mean—a broken intermediate trend. I'd be a buyer of AAPL above 300 and would flip cautious on a close below that level; for AMZN, I need to see RSI reclaim 50 and price stabilize above 240 before getting constructive.

views.note: Strongest technical profile in the universe: +9.3% above 50d, +15.9% above 200d, only -2.5% from highs, solid relative strength; would reassess on a close below 300.
Parabolic 12w move of +40% with RSI 68.3 near overbought—trend is undeniable but stretched; I'd trail a stop near 375 (roughly the 50d area) and respect the trend until it breaks.
RSI 37.8, -9.1% in one week, -10.1% relative strength vs SPY over 4w—this is active selling pressure and I want no part of it until price stabilizes above 240.
Trading -8.7% below 200d mean with -23.1% drawdown from 52w high and negative relative strength; broken intermediate uptrend with no sign of a base forming yet.
Extraordinary 26w gain of +57.6% and +39.6% above 200d mean makes this massively extended; RSI 55 is moderate but the mean-reversion risk is high—wait for a pullback toward 850.
Quiet strength: +4.4% last week, above both moving averages, low ATR of 2.0%, and only -6.6% from highs; a steady trend with low volatility, though 12w relative strength vs SPY is flat.
12w return of +19.4% and +21.2% above 200d are impressive, but the sharp 4w selloff of -7.4% and -8.2% relative weakness vs SPY suggest a pullback is underway; need to see 360 hold.
Strong 26w return of +30.6% but 12w return is -1.1% and relative strength vs SPY over 12w is -10.1%, suggesting the trend has stalled; sitting below 50d mean.
Persistent underperformance with -13.5% relative strength vs SPY over 12w, below 200d mean, and -12.4% drawdown; defensive name acting defenseless.
RSI 43.8 and -3.8% relative strength vs SPY over 4w show near-term weakness, but 12w return of +10.3% and position above 200d mean keep the intermediate trend intact; watching 195 as support.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names delivering durable, accelerating earnings power and those facing margin headwinds. NVDA's 2027Q1 print is staggering—$81.6B revenue (+85% YoY) with a 71.5% net margin and net income up 211% YoY on just $8.5B of total debt—making it the cleanest earnings story I can find. GOOGL delivered $110B in revenue (+21.8% YoY) with net income surging 81% to $62.6B and a 56.9% net margin, suggesting operating leverage is still expanding. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2% with flat net income and $77.9B in debt, signaling limited earnings durability. I would need to see XOM margins stabilize above 8% and UNH revenue reaccelerate above mid-single digits before reconsidering either name.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal leverage ($8.5B debt) is the strongest earnings profile in the universe.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B with 56.9% net margin and only $14.8B debt demonstrates powerful operating leverage and durable earnings expansion.
Revenue +18.3% YoY with 38.3% net margin and net income +23.1% on moderate $40.3B debt reflects consistent, high-quality compounding.
Net income surged 77% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, though $122.6B total debt warrants monitoring if capex intensity rises.
Solid +16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.7B debt load and slower earnings growth (+19.4%) versus peers temper enthusiasm.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% YoY with 14.6% margin is impressive for an industrial; I'd revisit if revenue growth decelerates below 10%.
Steady 10% revenue growth and 33% net margin are respectable for a bank, but the earnings trajectory (+12.6%) is modest relative to tech peers.
Revenue +7.4% and net income +4.3% with 18.5% margin is stable but unexciting; I see no catalyst for margin expansion.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin signals severe earnings compression; I need margins above 8% to reconsider.
Revenue grew just 2% YoY with flat net income and $77.9B debt, pointing to stalled earnings power and limited margin of safety.

memos.headline: Fed Paused at 3.75% but Sticky 3.8% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Squeeze Duration and Favor Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—upper bound unchanged at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, with the effective rate flat at 3.63%. The problem is inflation: CPI is running 3.8% YoY as of April, well above target, while the 10-year yield has surged 42 bps over three months to 4.55%, flattening the 10y-2y spread to just 0.42 pp. The labor market is stable at 4.3% unemployment, giving the Fed no urgency to ease further. This regime—paused policy, above-target inflation, rising long rates—is hostile to duration-sensitive growth equities and constructive for banks earning wider net interest margins and for energy/staples that benefit from nominal pricing power. A CPI print dropping below 3.0% YoY or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would shift my call toward resumed easing and a growth-stock tilt.

views.note: Pause regime with a positively sloped curve at 42 bps and elevated long rates supports bank NII; JPM is the highest-quality way to play this.
Sticky inflation and nominal GDP resilience favor energy cash flows; stable unemployment supports demand.
Defensive staples with pricing power are a reasonable hedge while CPI runs near 4% and the Fed stays on hold.
Long-duration consumer tech is pressured by 10-year yields at 4.55% and rising; multiple compression risk is real.
Highest-duration name in the universe faces headwinds from the 42 bp backup in the 10-year over three months.
Recurring enterprise revenue provides some cushion, but rising discount rates cap upside; I stay neutral until rates stabilize.
AWS margins help but consumer segment is cyclically exposed; rising long rates and sticky inflation keep me sidelined.
Ad revenue is macro-sensitive; stable employment is supportive but rising yields limit re-rating potential.
Classic cyclical benefits from stable employment but faces margin pressure from input-cost inflation at 3.8% YoY CPI.
Defensive healthcare but regulatory uncertainty and limited macro tailwinds in a pause regime keep conviction low.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: GOOGL and CAT Surged, MSFT and NVDA Sold Off — Narrative Momentum Favors the Winners
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. GOOGL (+10.0%) and CAT (+9.9%) posted outsized positive reactions on their Q1 results, suggesting a genuine narrative shift that likely attracted incremental positive media coverage; however, five weeks have passed since those prints, so much of the good news is priced. MSFT's -3.9% earnings-day drop and NVDA's -1.8% decline stand out as negative tone inflections, and MSFT's subsequent director departure filing on 5/14 adds a secondary negative headline. UNH's +7.0% earnings pop was notable, but the 5/11 Reg FD disclosure introduces ambiguity about forward guidance tone. GOOGL's 6/4 material definitive agreement filing is a fresh catalyst that could sustain positive coverage momentum, making it the name where I have the most conviction on continued favorable sentiment.

views.note: A +10% earnings pop followed by a material agreement filing on 6/4 suggests sustained positive narrative momentum that may not yet be fully priced.
The +9.9% earnings reaction was the second-largest in the universe, but five weeks of digestion and no fresh positive catalysts temper my conviction.
A -3.9% earnings-day selloff combined with a director departure two weeks later creates a negative tone trajectory that likely persists.
Two director departures in quick succession plus a -1.8% earnings reaction point to a souring narrative despite the AI tailwind.
The +7.0% earnings pop was strong, but the 5/11 Reg FD disclosure introduces uncertainty about forward tone and I lack clarity on its content.
A clean +3.2% earnings reaction and no subsequent negative filings leave sentiment mildly positive, though the move is modest.
A -0.8% earnings reaction was negligible, and the high volume of routine filings since then generates noise without a clear directional tone shift.
A -1.0% earnings reaction is mildly negative but not decisive; subsequent filings are routine governance items with no sentiment signal.
A tepid +0.8% earnings reaction suggests the market was already positioned for the result; no strong tone shift either way.
A +1.7% earnings pop is modestly positive but unremarkable for a defensive name; sentiment is stable, not inflecting.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Surging Oil Prices Signal Persistent Geopolitical Risk Despite Falling VIX
memos.body: I see a striking divergence between market-implied volatility (VIX at 15.40, down 27% over three months) and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 363.49, which has surged nearly 58% over the same period. This tells me credit and equity markets are complacent relative to the structural policy risks still in play—likely around trade/tariff escalation, energy security, and export controls. WTI crude at $96.83, up nearly 30% in three months despite a recent 12% pullback, points to supply-side tightness that could reflect sanctions enforcement or OPEC+ discipline; either way it is a tailwind for XOM and a headwind for input-cost-sensitive names like PG and CAT. I have higher conviction on energy exposure and financials (JPM benefits from steeper curves and elevated deal flow around sanctions compliance), and I am cautious on hardware-exposed tech names like NVDA and AAPL where export-control risk to China remains a structural overhang. A reversal in the policy uncertainty index below 250 or a concrete US-China semiconductor trade agreement would change my view on the tech names.

views.note: WTI up ~30% in 3 months supports earnings; energy security concerns keep supply tight and policy supportive for domestic producers.
Flattening but positive yield curve (10y-2y at 0.42pp) and tight HY spreads (2.74%) support bank earnings; elevated policy uncertainty drives advisory and compliance revenue.
Policy uncertainty index up 58% in 3 months likely reflects ongoing export-control tightening toward China, a structural headwind for NVDA's data-center GPU shipments.
Supply-chain concentration in China and elevated policy uncertainty warrant caution, but consumer demand resilience and low VIX limit near-term downside.
Surging crude raises input costs for consumer staples; two Reg FD filings in April may signal guidance adjustments, keeping me on the sideline.
Infrastructure spending tailwinds are offset by elevated policy uncertainty and potential tariff exposure on steel/components; two recent 8-Ks suggest management is actively managing disclosure.
Three 8-K filings in under a month suggest active regulatory engagement; antitrust and data-sovereignty risks are real but less acute than semiconductor export controls.

plan.summary: We tilt toward names where multiple analysts agree on favorable positioning: JPM (macro + geopolitical + technical), GOOGL (fundamentals + sentiment), AAPL (technical strength despite macro headwinds), and a modest NVDA allocation on extraordinary fundamentals despite sentiment/macro drags. We hold meaningful cash (~35%) given rising long rates, sticky inflation, and elevated policy uncertainty.

plans.rationale: Strongest cross-analyst agreement: macro analyst favors banks in a pause/positive-curve regime, geopolitics analyst highlights advisory/compliance tailwinds, and technicals show quiet strength above both moving averages with low volatility. Sizing at max reflects three-way convergence.
plans.changes_my_mind: 10-year yield drops below 4.10% (curve flattens to near zero or inverts) or unemployment spikes above 4.6%, undermining the bank NII thesis.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst highlights net income +81% YoY with 56.9% net margin; sentiment analyst notes sustained positive narrative from +10% earnings pop and fresh 6/4 material agreement filing. Technical pullback of -7.4% over 4w creates a better entry, though we need 360 to hold.
plans.changes_my_mind: Weekly close below 360 (key technical support) or a negative antitrust ruling headline that shifts the narrative.

plans.rationale: Technical analyst's highest-conviction long (0.82): cleanest relative strength profile, only -2.5% from 52w high, above both moving averages. Sentiment is mildly positive. Sized down because macro analyst warns rising 10y yields pressure duration and geopolitics analyst flags China supply-chain risk.
plans.changes_my_mind: Weekly close below 300 invalidates the technical thesis; a new China export-control announcement would add structural risk.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst's top pick (0.95): revenue +85% YoY, 71.5% net margin, net income +211%. However, sentiment is negative (director departures, -1.8% earnings reaction), macro analyst warns on duration, and geopolitics analyst flags export-control risk. Sized small to respect the conflict but capture extraordinary earnings power.
plans.changes_my_mind: A concrete new US export-control rule targeting AI GPUs to China, or a weekly close below 195 (technical support).

plans.rationale: Geopolitics analyst is constructive (WTI +30% in 3 months, supply tightness) and macro analyst sees sticky inflation supporting energy cash flows. However, fundamentals analyst flags severe earnings compression (net income -46% YoY) and technicals show a stalled trend below 50d mean. Small position reflects the conflict.
plans.changes_my_mind: WTI crude drops below $85 or net margins fail to recover above 8% in the next quarterly print.
